_readme: Single source of truth for the GordonOS dynamic task pipeline.
tools/gen-task-asm.ps1 turns this into tools/assemble-tasks.asm and tools/gen-fixups.asm;
tools/build-reu.ps1 seeds the REU filesystem from the same list.
name   - label prefix + temp binary base name (tasks-out/temp/<name>.{base,shift,check}.bin)
source - task wrapper .asm, imported by assemble-tasks.asm
origin - nominal assembly origin; pages are added per variant (origin+0/$100/$200)
out    - final binary under tasks-out/ (defaults to <name>.bin)
fsName - filename in the REU filesystem (.tsk/.com/.lib)
note   - optional; emitted as the block comment in both generated files

tasks.name: basic
tasks.note: program storage is the REU working file (no pool RAM block); footprint 109/109 -- code 64 + eager gfx/FP + startup-lazy filesys.lib, see tools/check-pool-budget.ps1

tasks.name: maze
tasks.note: re-runnable

tasks.name: gfxdemo
tasks.note: declares gfx.lib

tasks.name: fpdemo
tasks.note: declares fp.lib

tasks.name: spirog
tasks.note: integer spirograph; takes args R r d col

tasks.name: shell
tasks.note: reentrant; boot loads this first

tasks.name: ps
tasks.note: declares string.lib

tasks.name: copy
tasks.note: runtime kMalloc buffer, freed on exit

tasks.name: banner
tasks.note: 2-page runtime kMalloc row buffer, freed on exit

tasks.name: edit
tasks.note: KF_NOT_EVICTABLE + KF_RE_RUNNABLE + KF_TAKES_ARGS ($69); document chunks and the clipboard are runtime kMalloc blocks

tasks.name: sidplay
tasks.note: thin wrapper over sid.lib: finds/loads the .mus via filesys.lib + kMalloc, calls kSidPlay(kPtr=tune, kArg=delay, kArg+1=repeats), frees, exits; on failure reports on a temporary screen and waits for a key. libMask $0022 (filesys bit 1 + sid bit 5), ZP $02 len 9

tasks.name: sidrst
tasks.note: zero fixups

tasks.name: speed
tasks.note: declares the machine's speed; scales blink/keyrpt and feeds sysSpeedShift

tasks.name: fstest
tasks.note: declares filesys.lib; runtime self-test for the FS bank boundary - type fstest

tasks.name: ipctest
tasks.note: declares ipc.lib; the ipc.lib runtime self-test (keep - the counterpart of fstest) - spawns two thread producers (channels 1 and 3) and consumes both interleaved, so the backpressure wait and the channel recovery after SYS_SLEEP are both exercised; expect `ipc PASS`

tasks.name: sprdemo
tasks.note: no libs - eight bouncing balls: all 8 sprite slots, REU sheet art (ball.spr), wall + ball-ball collisions, one update per displayed frame

tasks.name: godzi
tasks.note: no libs, KF_TAKES_ARGS, single-instance (owns the SID, so a second run is refused) - port of reference/godzi.asm + reference/main.asm: boat walker crosses x=256 (two overlapping layers, black rigging over a light-blue hull), Godzilla flaps between two poses (four slots, REU art boat.spr/godzi.spr, one update per displayed frame); spawns + restarts sidplay for music (commodo 2 in mode 1, fsonata 2 in mode 2), and on q kills it + spawns sidrst (killing a SID player leaves the chip holding its note)

tasks.name: gortris
tasks.note: KF_NOT_EVICTABLE ($41), libMask $0022 (filesys + sid); port of wiebow/tetris.c64 (MIT) - a 10x20 board in the task image, the reference's own 4x4 piece frames and its Select/Animate/Block*/CheckLines/FlashLines/RemoveLines logic, rendered as 8-byte block glyphs; attract loop (4 screens on its 254-frame delay) -> level select (its 0-9 grid, flashing digit) -> play -> game over -> attract (the game over runs the reference's animation: the well fills with blocks a row a frame, is held full ~3 s, empties, and then the text is printed inside the well); hi scores = the reference's 3-entry table (7-char name + 3 BCD score bytes) kept in the REU FS as gortris.hi, shown on the select screen, checked at game over (a tie does not displace), with its own yielding name editor (kReadString spins) that types into the 7-cell field under the kernel's blinking block cursor (kEnableCursor/kBlinkReset; a key from kReadKey is a SCREEN CODE, so the letters are $01-$1A and a 'printable = >= $20' test discards all of them); this is why the task HOLDS filesys.lib for the session instead of handing it back like sidplay); level rule = its 10 lines/level, fall delay -4 per level floored at 4, line score x(level+1); music is sid.lib called DIRECTLY by a thread child it spawns (ZP $02-$0A declared by that child): the tune is kMalloc'd from the REU FS at startup (tetris.mus -- our own three-voice SID arrangement of the Tetris theme Korobeiniki: the melody and bass line were read from a MIDI made from a fan piano sheet (NinSheetMusic sheet 574, 'Tetris - A Theme (Korobeiniki)', piano arrangement by Olimar12345, credited there to Hirokazu Tanaka's game arrangement, Nintendo (C) 1989 -- see NOTICE), the chords fitted from the notes sounding, and the SID voicing, form and mix ours, by tools/gen-mus.py; because a `.sid` is a program, not a score, so no converter exists) -- that file plays ONCE (no HED/TAL loop in it) and the child passes kSidPlay repeats = 0 so the PLAYER repeats it, which is why `run sidplay tetris` stops after one pass; `m` toggles the music from any screen (the play panel shows 'music off', and the mute survives focus and mode changes because gtMusicStart refuses while gtMusOff is set), filesys.lib NOT handed back (kLibHold is one-way and the hi-score table has to be written), hushed on focus loss and the child reaped + buffer freed on exit; attract screens show for 1016 displayed frames (~20 s) each; owns the display + kbFocus; keys: , . move, a s turn, ENTER step down (1 a row), SPACE hard drop to the floor + settle (2 a row, this port's own move), p pause, q quit; also reads the reference's joystick (port 2, UNTESTED: UP rotate-CCW, DOWN soft drop, LEFT/RIGHT move, FIRE rotate-CW/start) and ports its INPUT repeat tuning -- INPUTDELAY 10 frames between repeats, halved for the drop keys, adjustable on the select screen with '-'/'+'

tasks.name: grknoid
tasks.note: KF_NOT_EVICTABLE ($41), libMask $00A2 (sprite.lib + filesys.lib + sid.lib) - gorkanoid, an Arkanoid/Breakout game: a paddle sprite (gkpad.spr, x-expanded 24->48px) under a wall of glyph bricks on the task's own hires-text surface; the wall is a 48-entry byte array in the task image (0 = a gap, 1-3 = the hits to break the brick) and is the AUTHORITY -- the drawn cells are presentation and nothing reads the surface back; the paddle follows the HELD key (kernel data keybHeld, a LEVEL) one step per DISPLAYED frame, with the step ACCELERATING 1 -> 3 px while the same direction is held (16 displayed frames a gear, reset by a release or a reversal), with 'j' 'k' SPACE and the port-2 joystick (DDRA dance under SEI, bits tested individually) feeding one input byte, and the buttons taken from its newly-down bits; the paddle's x is stored as an offset from its left stop so the whole run fits one byte and kSpritePos's ninth bit is the carry out of the same add; the ball is sprite 1 (gkball.spr, an 8x8 disc in the sheet's TOP-LEFT corner so the sprite position IS the box -- 8 because a 6px box can only be a rounded square) flown in 8.8 fixed point -- x three bytes because 24..344 does not fit one, y two, velocities signed with the sign carried above the fraction, integration an adc chain and a bounce a two's-complement negation; the paddle's angle comes from the hit offset scaled by 8, floored at $0060 so the ball can never climb straight up, plus THE ENGLISH: half the paddle's speed added when it is moving into the ball, using the direction it ACTUALLY travelled (a paddle held against a wall contributes nothing); the bricks are 8 to a row, 4 cells each, so a row is exactly 32px and a level table row is exactly FOUR nibble-packed bytes (two bricks a byte, the left one low -- $11 is two one-hit bricks, and the five levels are six source lines each that ARE the wall); a brick's colour carries BOTH its damage and its position -- the table is indexed by hit points*2 + the column parity, so each hit-point group owns a PAIR of alternating hues (red/orange 3 hits, light green/green 2, yellow/cyan 1); the ball's brick test takes the 2x2 cell block at the ball's own cell, first hit wins, and reverses vx when the hit cell's COLUMN differs from the ball's CENTRE cell and vy when its ROW does (a corner does both) -- the reference this is ported from reversed only vy and so could never break a brick with the ball's side; a hit pays 5 when it only cracks a brick and 10 x the level when it breaks one, kept in 16-bit BINARY and printed by repeated subtraction, never in decimal mode (the timer IRQ does arithmetic, and a keyboard scan landing inside a `sed` window computes a wrong key index -- one of the wrong keys is q, which quits); the frame wall and the HUD are drawn once and no rule ever writes the last row; the game is a MODE MACHINE (attract, play, over) and the attract loop is the only place the controls are shown -- four screens on a 1016-frame delay inside a closed box that covers the whole surface, any key starting a game (and the closed box's bottom edge has to go through kBlitChar, because a print into the last cell of the last row wraps and scrolls the whole surface); five lives, a drawn DEATH LINE across the field's floor (the last pixel line of the cell row GK_BALL_DEADY names, one pixel line per cell through gkGlyphDead), and a game over that is a SHELL screen -- the field cleared, the same box up -- which checks the run's score against gortris's own three-row BCD table (grknoid.hi in the REU FS, the name typed into the row under the kernel's block cursor, saved find-delete-save because the FS delete is a tombstone); the kernel's key queue is consumed only by a LATCH that waits for the keys to be released first (a per-frame idle test drains the very press it is waiting for), and the game-over screen drops back to the attract loop on its own after GK_RETURN_DELAY of an idle keyboard and a displayed surface, while the NAME ENTRY never times out at all (it is a data-entry step: RETURN is what commits the typed name, and the save runs only after it, so the screen waits for the player rather than storing something they never finished); the ball's colour PULSES through the palette's greys (white, light, medium, dark, and back) one shade every 8 displayed frames, stepped from the ball's own frame tail so it freezes with the game and costs one kSpriteReg per shade rather than per frame; the SERVE'S SPEED RAMPS WITH THE LEVEL -- gkLaunch takes vx from gkVxTab (level 1 is the GK_VXMIN floor, +$18 a level, so level 5 is exactly twice level 1) and DERIVES vy as -2 * vx, which holds the launch angle at 26.6 degrees from the vertical on every level, capped by GK_VYMAX ($0180 = 1.5 px/frame, the number gkBallPaddle's y-band proof already assumes) with four asserts pinning the shape so a steeper ramp fails the build instead of the play test, and the level is on the HUD as lv at column 34 with its digit at 37 because a ramped speed a player cannot see is indistinguishable from a bounce going well; and the music is THREE CGSC tunes (katmand/immig/firstdt -- the Compute's Gazette Sid Collection, the archive written for the Sidplayer sid.lib ports) played one per mode by a thread child the task spawns and reaps: katmand in the attract loop, immig in a game, and firstdt ONCE at game over, after which the child hands the attract tune back by itself; the task kMallocs ONE 18-page tune buffer at startup and keeps it for the whole session, sized for the largest tune (katmand); the child loads each mode's tune INTO that buffer, so nothing is allocated or freed on a mode change (a per-tune malloc/free cycle fragments the pool, and an 18-page request then cannot be satisfied), and filesys.lib stays held for the whole session because the score table is written and the child reads a tune file on every switch; a SID the child is REFUSED (another task owns the chip) is not a failure -- the tune is KEPT and the play is retried about once a second, so the music returns by itself, while a tune that will not LOAD -- missing, unreadable, or longer than the buffer -- falls back to the attract tune and then goes quiet WITHOUT a retry, because a kMalloc retry can evict another task; the game-over screen's tune is its CLOCK: it waits for the one-shot to finish (the child sets gkMusDone) and leaves then, or at once on a key, and GK_RETURN_DELAY is only the fallback for a screen with no tune to wait for; losing the display freezes the game (no mode step, keybHeld kept in step, q focused-only) but does NOT hush the music, deliberately unlike gortris

tasks.name: grview
tasks.note: KF_TAKES_ARGS - the .pic viewer: `run grview hires` opens hires.pic (the suffix is appended, as sidplay appends .mus, so the base name is <= 7); 'm' reinterprets the same bytes in the other mode and any other key exits; a failure takes a screen of its own and waits for a key, sidplay-style; declares gfx.lib + filesys.lib

tasks.name: grpaint
tasks.note: KF_TAKES_ARGS, SINGLE-INSTANCE (NOT KF_RE_RUNNABLE: its 71-page live footprint means two copies plus the shell are the whole pool, so a second run would evict the copy that is running) - the 1351 paint program. The mouseKind gate comes first (off -> a screen of its OWN with a dark grey border, '? mouse off - run mouse 1351', held until a key -- the sidplay pattern, never a shared-shell print), then kAllocScreen takes a bitmap canvas in the MODE AND PALETTE the run resolved (the colour arguments for a new picture, the file's own header for a load, both settled BEFORE the alloc so the surface is never re-coloured afterwards) and the alloc hands it back already cleared, kDisableCursor + the SEI-wrapped kBlinkReset/kSwitchView hand-over shows it without baking the shell's blink block. The pointer is TWO SPRITES stamping ONE shape: pointer.spr carries two hires frames of the classic arrow-pointer silhouette, frame 0 the interior taking the ink (and, while the palette is up, the colour of the swatch under the pointer) and frame 1 the ring taking a FIXED colour, each bound once via kSpriteSheet (a sheet record is per sprite, so the one file needs two calls); it is positioned once per DISPLAYED frame off frameCount at sprite (canvas x + 24, canvas y + 50) -- the window's left edge and its first raster line -- moved by mouse.lib's SIGNED deltas (MOUSE_READ -> kArg+MOUSE_DELTA_*, the y one negated because the 1351's y runs opposite to the screen's), clamped to 0..319 by 0..199. The per-frame reading is not trusted on its own: the pot noise makes a sample read one count high, so the frame is followed as offsets from its first sample and moved by the change in their MINIMUM, which is the reading with no noise on it. Painting: the left button (PA4 of $DC00, the fire line, ACTIVE LOW) draws the segment from where the previous frame's stroke ended to where this frame moved the pointer, one kPlot per pixel -- kPlot is the call that commits a cell's matrix high nibble, so in hires the stroke shows the ink. The walk is the task's own Bresenham with the error held below the major span, which draws a line steeper than 45 degrees as the run of pixels it is rather than a dotted diagonal; a press is an EVENT, so a click marks exactly one pixel, and a pointer moved with the button up writes nothing. Both endpoints are clamped, and the walk only steps towards the destination, so no clip is needed anywhere. 'q' ASKS BEFORE IT LOSES WORK: with the canvas as the file holds it, 'q' drains the key queue, clears the sprite enable and SYS_EXITs (no kFreeScreen) at once; with something drawn since the last save, the first 'q' only raises the band if it is down and starts the SAVE tile FLASHING (gpFlash: once a frame, phase from one bit of frameCount -- 32 frames each way, 0.8 Hz -- re-reading the band's matrix from its file and re-marking on a change), and it is the SAVE tile's own press -- which saves and stays, clearing both GP_WARN and the flash -- or 'q' again WHILE THE BAND IS UP (gpQuitAsk, GP_WARN: a dismissed band is a question nobody can see, so the next 'q' raises it again) that ends it. The palette (step 4.6) is the right button HELD: the canvas's BOTTOM TWO cell rows become a full-width UI band, with the sixteen 8x8-cell swatches filling its left 8 cells across BOTH rows -- colours 0-7 along the top, 8-15 along the bottom, in the order of the C64 palette (the swatch IS its colour). The band is two CELL rows -- a bitmap's cells are its memory, so a cell row of the screen is a contiguous 320-byte run and the band's two are one run of 640 -- and WHAT GOES IN IS A FILE: gpui.bin holds the band's own 640 pixel bytes then its 80 matrix bytes, built by tools/gen-ui.py from assets/ui/gpui.txt, so the task holds no picture and composes nothing. The right button keeps the band with two REU DMAs (gpDma: 640 pixel bytes at $3CC0 and 80 matrix bytes at $0798 into bank 0 $D000/$D280, free there so the filesystem loses no capacity), reads the file's two halves straight into those same addresses (kReuOpen at spawn for BOTH modes -- gpui.bin and gpui_mc.bin, a record each, selected by GP_MODE through gpUiRecOfs, so no press ever scans the directory, because a scan inside a press is a frame the pointer is not sampled over and a click can vanish in it -- then kReuReadAt), and the release puts the saved two runs back. Nothing in the band is ever written while the pointer moves over it: a swatch's colour IS its cell's matrix nibble, so a highlight drawn there would draw over the colour it marks -- the feedback is the pointer's INTERIOR, which takes the colour of the swatch under it (and the current ink off the palette). The release takes that colour as the ink, colours the interior with it and puts the band back; released off the palette it takes nothing. A press ON THE BAND but not on anything DRAWN is a press off the UI and puts the band away: in HIRES the four slot-chip columns are empty band, so the hit test offers no entry there rather than an entry whose press takes nothing. The pointer's ring is a FIXED colour, so the pointer stays visible even at ink 0. The tool tiles sit at the palette's right, each a 2x2-cell square: the PENCIL first -- it is what a fresh canvas starts with, so the default is the leftmost tile -- then the line, the box and the filled box. A tile's entry number (16 and up, counted on from the swatches) minus 16 IS its tool number, which is what makes the picker's arithmetic a subtraction and the mark's the same addition back. Each tile's picture carries its own 1px border with the tool's shape inside it, clear of the border, and the tool in use is told apart by COLOUR -- its four cells go white where the image holds them grey. The shape tools work click to click: the first click anchors and marks its pixel, the second draws from it. What the drawing click leaves behind is the tool's own business -- the LINE keeps the end it drew to, so EVERY click after the first draws from where the last line ended and a run of lines is one click each, while the BOX and the FILLED BOX CONSUME their anchor, so a rectangle is two clicks, every time. The line is drawn with the SAME Bresenham the pencil uses (the anchor becomes GP_LAST and gpSeg commits it, so one walk serves both tools). The box and the filled box hand kBox/kFillBox the two corners sorted into kArg (X1, Y1, width, height; the x pair a signed 16-bit difference, the y pair an unsigned compare of the two rows), and then colour their cells themselves: kLine, kBox and kFillBox all go through gxPix, which writes the PIXEL only, so the matrix nibble that decides what colour the shape shows is written by a walk of the CELL grid, one kPlot per cell -- the outline's two edge columns and two edge rows, every row for the fill. The walk's state (GP_WK_*: the two edges, the two rows, the cell counts and the live counters) cannot live in kArg, because kPlot clobbers it between two cells. A held button cannot commit twice, which is why the LEFT button keeps a previous-frame byte (GP_PREV) while the right button deliberately does not need one. Only the display owner may open the palette (it reads the framebuffer directly), a stroke in progress blocks it for the PENCIL only (a shape tool draws nothing until its second click), and a left press closes the palette before it draws. The canvas's matrix is filled from the palette at alloc -- (ink << 4) | paper in hires, where a cell's colour IS its matrix nibbles. Every mark is then CLAIMED (gpClaim, step 4.15): in MC kPlot writes the pixel's 2-bit VALUE only and the colour it shows is the cell's own byte, so the mark gives the cell the pen's colour for that value (the high nibble for value 1, the low one for 2, the colour RAM for 3, nothing for 0 -- $D021 is one register) and keeps the cell's other colour, exactly as the hires mark keeps the paper. That is what makes a stroke come out in the pen's colour on a loaded picture, whose cells carry their own two colours; kPlot running first, the shape walks claiming through gpCellMark, and a whole-canvas fill (gpCells) writing the same byte are what keep the two in step. The flood fill claims no cell: kFloodFill reports no list of the cells it filled. The command line is 'run grpaint <base> [border paper ink | border bg c1 c2 c3]': the COUNT of the values is the mode (three hires, five MC, none for the black-and-white defaults, anything else refused), a picture that already exists is a load whose own mode and colours win and which therefore refuses a colour argument, and the base name is at most 7 characters with no dot. UNDO AND REDO (steps 4.9/4.10): a ring of six canvas states in the REU's top full bank, $FB0000-$FBFFFF (bank 251), which reuFsCapacity stops one bank short of the top to reserve, so the filesystem can never grow into it -- a machine with fewer than 252 banks has no such bank and gets no history at all (gpUndoCap refuses and nothing is written). A state is a .pic PAYLOAD (gpPicTab's three regions at a file's own offsets, so a snapshot is three DMAs of the canvas's addresses) plus the mode and the four palette colours; six states are five steps each way and the seventh push drops the oldest. The ring holds the states EITHER SIDE of the one on screen, which is what makes redo the same walk as undo. GP_U_HEAD is the state the canvas IS: every action that changes it ends in gpUndoPush (a stroke's release, the line's SECOND click, a shape's commit, the fill, a text entry put away with the caret off the canvas, and the CLEAR tile, an MC palette press and the MODE tile through gpUndoPushBand, which takes the band down for the snapshot because its own rows are the canvas's bottom two). The push stores the canvas after the state on screen, so a new action after an undo DISCARDS the redo tail, and a mark that is on the canvas but not in a state (the line's anchor click, a stroke still under the button) is taken off first by gpDropMark -- it is not a step, so it never enters the ring, and the press that took it off stops there (C=1), so a step never takes off the unfinished mark and the action before it together. A step restores the pixels, the cells, the mode and the palette, and sets GP_DIRTY -- and never the pen: the tool, the ink, the slot and the value are the user's, not the picture's. Every entry point is display-guarded, since a snapshot READS the framebuffer, the matrix and the colour RAM, which are the canvas only while it is the surface on screen. The gestures are u and r on the keyboard (the text pen has the keys while it is down) and the band's two arrows: undo across its TOP cell row and redo across the bottom one, in the last two columns -- 16x8 each and STACKED, because a full 16x16 icon would want four columns and only two are free after the tiles and the four slot chips, so the picker reads the band's ROW there rather than its column, and either arrow is MARKED WHITE while the ring has a step that way (HEAD against GP_U_OLD and GP_U_NEW, folded into gpMark so every path that re-reads the band's matrix marks them). A mark that no state holds -- the line's anchor click, a stroke still under the button -- is NOT a step: it colours no arrow, it never enters the ring, and it is taken off by gpDropMark, which shows HEAD again (HEAD does not contain it) with GP_DRAW cleared and C=1 so a step press stops there (one press one thing; the next press is the step). The band's own opening drops a LINE's waiting anchor before it reads the band, so the arrows always describe the ring, while the band comes back at the step's shared tail. Declares sprite.lib + mouse.lib + gfx.lib + filesys.lib

tasks.name: granim
tasks.note: KF_TAKES_ARGS - the REU animation film player: `run granim llama` opens llama.inf (the suffix appended in place, like grview's, so the base name is <= 7) and plays the chunks it names. The manifest carries the rate, the palette, the frame count, the chunk shape and the first chunk's name, so the task knows no particular film; the chunk number is bumped IN PLACE in that name, so no number is ever formatted on the machine. A chunk is a run of whole .pic records and a frame goes straight to $0400/$D800/$2000 in six kReuReadAt calls of at most 2000 bytes, and THE ORDER IS MATRIX, COLOUR RAM, THEN PIXELS TOP ROW DOWN -- that order is what makes a whole-screen rewrite tear-free, because the beam reads a line's matrix and colour before that line's pixels, so every write lands ahead of the beam instead of behind it (the frame does not fit the border window and does not need to: 10,000 cycles of DMA against a 12,600-cycle visible period, the beam consuming 40 bytes a line where this writes 63). The clock is frameCount, the display's own 50.1 Hz, never the scheduler tick, with a fractional accumulator whose step is the film's own rate -- so 24 fps alternates two and three display frames a film frame instead of drifting into a stutter. Losing the display to an F-key switch PAUSES the film rather than writing a frame into another task's surface, and it resumes from the next frame because the one on show is the one that was saved. 'q' exits, SPACE holds it, '+'/'-' change speed (the accumulator's step is the rate shifted); a failure takes a screen of its own and waits for a key, sidplay-style; declares gfx.lib + filesys.lib

tasks.name: timelib
tasks.note: lib 0 (eager), relocatable

tasks.name: filesyslib
tasks.note: lib 1 (lazy), relocatable

tasks.name: gfxlib
tasks.note: lib 2 (lazy), relocatable

tasks.name: fplib
tasks.note: lib 3 (eager), relocatable; note the out name is fp.bin, not fplib.bin

tasks.name: stringlib
tasks.note: lib 4 (lazy), relocatable

tasks.name: sidlib
tasks.note: lib 5 (lazy), relocatable; the Sidplayer (sidplay.inc) behind kSidPlay/kSidHush; callers must declare ZP $02-$0A

tasks.name: ipclib
tasks.note: lib 6 (lazy), relocatable; IPC pipe (kIpcPost/kIpcPick) as a 128-byte ring in the library's own shared data, lock-free SPSC, no caller ZP

tasks.name: spritelib
tasks.note: lib 7 (eager), relocatable; the sprite API behind four call entries (sheet/frame/pos/reg) -- per-task sprite state, handed over with the display (docs/lib-sprite.md)

tasks.name: mouselib
tasks.note: lib 8 (eager), relocatable; the 1351 reader behind one dispatching entry (kMouseCall, call 41): MOUSE_READ publishes raw x/y and signed deltas in kArg+0..3 with the buttons in A, MOUSE_ENABLE primes, MOUSE_DISABLE refuses. Reads $D419/$D41A with the PRA $DC00 select and DDRA per bit under SEI, and never consults mouseKind (docs/lib-mouse.md)

tasks.name: mousetest
tasks.note: declares LIB_MOUSE - the 1351 protocol readout (docs/lib-mouse.md): reads $D419/$D41A directly, with the PRA $DC00 multiplexer select and DDRA per bit under SEI, and prints the raw POT byte, the position mod 64, the delta since the last sample, the running total and PA5..PA0 of $DC00 on the shell's SHARED screen, refreshed once every 4 displayed frames. 'l' takes the same sample through mouse.lib instead, 'p' switches control port and 'h' cycles the hold; any other key exits. It takes the keyboard focus with kSwitchView (the format pattern) so the key read works, and does not consult mouseKind, so it diagnoses a machine the OS believes has no mouse. fsName is 9 chars: the REU FS caps a filename at 11, and the typed command is the FS name, not `name`

tasks.name: mouse
tasks.note: declares the pointer device: 'mouse 1351' / 'mouse off' write the kernel's mouseKind byte ($E530, 0 = off, 1 = 1351), and bare 'mouse' prints the current setting ('? mouse 1351 off' for an unrecognised argument, with the byte untouched). Policy only -- no libraries, no hardware, silent on success; a machine that has a 1351 declares it with a line in boot.bat, which the shipped image carries (docs/lib-mouse.md)
